t: Listen to a talk in an art history class.
Let's compare three movements from around the turn of the twentieth century.
They wanted to capture the changing effects of light, so they often painted outdoors, quickly, with loose brushstrokes.
Claude Monet, for example, painted the same haystacks again and again at different times of day, just to show how the light changed.
They weren't interested in what things looked like; they wanted to show emotion.
So they distorted shapes and used intense, unnatural colors.
Think of Edvard Munch's The Scream.
Painters like Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque broke objects into geometric shapes and showed them from several viewpoints at the same time, so you might see the front and the side of a face at once.
Those are the three ideas to keep apart.
